title: Higher module direct images on spaces preserve filtered colimits
statement: Work in the fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the canonical module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Suppose $f$ is quasi-compact (its pullback by every affine scheme over $Y$ has quasi-compact source) and quasi-separated (its relative diagonal is quasi-compact). Let $J$ be a small filtered category (nonempty, and every finite diagram admits a cocone), and $(M_j)_{j\in J}$ a diagram in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$. Its colimit is taken in all module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every integer $p\geq0$, the canonical map $$\varinjlim_{j\in J} R^pf_*M_j\longrightarrow R^pf_*\left(\varinjlim_{j\in J} M_j\right)$$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules. Here $R^pf_*$ is computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The maps are induced by the colimit injections. Neither quasi-coherence of the $M_j$ nor quasi-compactness of $X$ or $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07U6, lemma-colimit-cohomology, module version via sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree) on slice sites and module sheafification.

proof.text: Use the enlarged etale ringed sites $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$ in the common sheaf universe. Their equivalences with the small sites extend structure sheaves and module sheaves. The base-change functor $u(V)=X\times_YV$ presents the canonical ringed-topos morphism. The chart-limit comparison identifies its module direct image with precisely the specified $f_*$. Equivalences preserve colimits by their universal property and preserve injectives, so derived direct image computed using these models represents the same functor. Module sheaves over each ring sheaf are Grothendieck and hence have enough injectives; abelian sheaves have enough injectives as well.

Put $M=\varinjlim_J M_j$ and $F_j=(M_j)_{ab}$. Exact scalar forgetting preserves all small colimits, so $M_{ab}=\varinjlim_J F_j$ with the original coprojections. All colimits here and below are sheaf colimits, not sectionwise presheaf colimits.

For any object $W$ of $\mathcal C_X$, restriction of abelian sheaves to $\mathcal C_X/W$ preserves colimits. Indeed set $\lambda:\mathcal C_X/W\to\mathcal C_X$ to be the forgetful functor and $\beta(T)=(T\times_XW\to W)$. The universal property of the fibre product gives $\lambda\dashv\beta$. Precomposition with $\lambda$ preserves sheaves since slice coverings are underlying coverings; precomposition with $\beta$ preserves sheaves since covers and their overlaps pull back to covers and overlaps. The adjoint-continuous-restriction theorem therefore makes restriction $\lambda^s$ a left adjoint to $\beta^s$. Left adjoints preserve the given $J$-colimit. Thus $(\varinjlim_JF_j)|_W=\varinjlim_J(F_j|_W)$ with the restricted coprojections.

proof.text: Let $V\to Y$ be an affine etale scheme and put $W=X\times_YV$. It is quasi-compact by the stated affine-test hypothesis on $f$. To check quasi-separatedness on affine tests, take affine schemes $T,T'$ mapping to $W$. Their maps to $V$ give an affine scheme $T\times_VT'$. The map $T\times_WT'\to T\times_VT'$ is the base change of $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$, hence its source is quasi-compact by the quasi-compactness hypothesis on $\Delta_f$ and this affine test. This is exactly the affine-test criterion for the absolute diagonal of $W$ to be quasi-compact. Thus $W$ is qcqs. This checks the definitions directly and uses no qcqs assumption on $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 07U6 (lemma-colimit-cohomology), proof: affine V has qcqs pullback; scheme-test verification of that assertion

proof.text:
The enlarged-site localization identifies $\mathcal C_X/W$ with the etale site of $W$ up to the stated equivalence. Cohomology over $W$ is cohomology of the restricted abelian sheaf on that slice, naturally in coefficients. Apply qcqs-space cohomology continuity to $W$ and $(F_j|_W)_{j\in J}$, which is a small filtered diagram. Using step 3, its canonical comparison is
$\varinjlim_JH^p(W,F_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(W,M_{ab})$.
The module/abelian evaluation comparison at the object $W$ is natural in the module and is the identity in degree zero. Apply it to every $M_j$ and to $M$. Naturality for each coprojection $M_j\to M$ identifies the preceding map with
$\varinjlim_JH^p_{\mathrm{Mod}}(W,M_j)\to H^p_{\mathrm{Mod}}(W,M)$.
Thus this specific module-cohomology comparison is an isomorphism. No assertion that a forgotten injective module is injective is used.

Every object of $\mathcal C_Y$ has a cover by affine etale schemes, by taking a scheme chart and its affine-open cover. Use these objects as $\mathcal B$ in the ringed-site higher-image colimit criterion. Step 5 verifies its comparison hypothesis for every member of $\mathcal B$, with $u(V)=W$, in the fixed degree $p$. Step 1 supplies the ringed-site model and enough injectives. The criterion now gives the required isomorphism of structure-module sheaves. Under the equivalences in step 1 it is the canonical comparison in the statement: on each $j$-th colimit leg it is $R^pf_*(M_j\to M)$, because the criterion and all coefficient comparisons above use those same coprojections. Equality on all colimit legs identifies the maps. The argument works for every $p\geq0$.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NO-b879f67f8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no fixes. Statement and route: the item's statement is unchanged and matches Stacks 07U6 (spaces-cohomology.tex lemma-colimit-cohomology, read lines 480-511), upgraded to module coefficients. Its six steps follow the 07U6 proof, with modules in place of abelian sheaves.

New node: lem-sfb-ringed-site-higher-image-colimit-criterion is the module form of Stacks 0H7B (sites-cohomology.tex lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit, read lines 2822-2852). Its proof would go: R^pf_* is the sheafification of V -> H^p(u(V),-) (Stacks 072W, module form); module sheafification is a left adjoint; and a presheaf map that is an isomorphism on a covering collection B becomes an isomorphism after sheafification. So the statement is true without filteredness of J and without fibre-product closure of B, as the node says. I tested p=0, empty J, a singleton J and an empty B. The node is self-contained and every notion cites its definition node. It is a generic site-level tool smaller than the item, not a restatement. Greps for 0H7B and 072W, and a scan of statements combining R^q f_* with colim, found no duplicate.

Steps:
- Step 1: the enlarged ringed-site model and the chart-limit identification of D_f with Q_f give exactly the specified f_*. Enough injectives holds for any ring sheaf.
- Step 2: forgetting scalars commutes with colimits, by clause (3) of the cited node.
- Step 3: checked lambda left adjoint to beta and that both precompositions preserve sheaves, so restriction to the slice preserves the J-colimit.
- Step 4 (marked elementary): checked that T x_W T' is the pullback of Delta_f over the affine T x_V T'. The passage to the diagonal of W, absolute or over S, takes a few lines, so elementary is acceptable.
- Step 5: localization, the topos equivalence C_W with W_et, 073E on the qcqs space W with filtered J, and the module/abelian evaluation comparison, natural along each coprojection, give the module comparison.
- Step 6: affine etale schemes over Y form a covering collection by the a1 cover node, and the new criterion gives the item's map on the same colimit legs.

Batch-5 check: the four sec-trace-formula nodes (enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model, chart-limit-enlarged-sections, enlarged-site-scheme-density, chartwise-etale-permanence) are generic algebraic-space etale-site foundations cited by about 70 nodes, not trace-formula or Poincare-duality steps. lem-sfb-space-cohomology-filtered-colimit and lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover reach that chapter only through the definition def-trf-algebraic-space. Both conclusions: outside the assumptions, acceptable. The 13 off-unit tool_uses are generic infrastructure and are accepted.
